戴眼镜的露娜
Luna and the Big Star: A Story for Children
With High-Functioning Autistic Children
儿童情绪管理与性格培养绘本
第八辑 逆商培养

第八辑 逆商培养
戴眼镜的露娜
Luna and the Big Blur: A Story for Children
Who Wear Glasses (Revised Edition)
[美] 雪莉·戴 (Shirley Day) 著
[美] 唐·莫里斯 (Don Morris) 绘
赵丹 译
卓文如 译校

[P3] 露娜觉得她的名字像一条鱼，因为这总让她想起“吞拿鱼露娜”。
为什么我的名字不叫亚历克斯、雷切尔或者莎伦呢？

[P4] 露娜喜欢她的虎皮猫柏拉图，喜欢她那件带曲线和圆圆的黄色衬衫。她还喜欢卧室里拱形的窗户，透过它，露娜可以在睡觉时看到美丽的月亮。但是，露娜不喜欢自己的名字。还有一样东西她也不喜欢，一样她不能忽略的东西：

她的眼镜。

那副眼镜就架在她的鼻子上面，在她的脸上留下浅浅的凹（āo）痕。露娜在眼镜店里选了一副黄色镜框，上面还带着红色的小圆点，和她最喜欢的衬衫正好相配。尽管如此，露娜还是不喜欢她的眼镜。因为照镜子时，眼镜几乎遮住了她的整个脸。

[P5] 她用刘海盖住眼镜，好让它看起来不那么明显。
她还竖起大衣领子，试图挡住眼镜。
她甚至在走路的时候低着头。当然，这些都不怎么管用。
“哎哟！”

[P6] 露娜的妈妈开了一家礼品店，店里有很多稀奇古怪的东西，
有倒着走的时钟，还有一串看起来像奶油夹心饼干的灯。顾客们
见了都会说，“简直太不可思议了！”，
露娜的妈妈不用戴眼镜，
她的视力非常好。

[P7] 露娜的爸爸是一名高中数学老师，他的视力也非常好，也不用戴眼镜。
就连露娜的妹妹克里斯汀也不戴眼镜。
“我讨厌戴眼镜，”露娜抱怨道，“就算和我最喜欢的衣服相配，我的眼镜也太显眼了。这不公平！”

[P8] 一晚上，露娜睡得很香，她梦见自己到了月亮上，四周是巨大的向日葵，身边的池塘里有很多小鱼在水里跳。当它们跳出水面时，露娜能清楚地看到每一条鱼。
在梦里，露娜没有戴眼镜，这让她特别高兴。
“我能看见了！我不用戴眼镜了！”

[P9] 当露娜醒来时，她没有去找她的眼镜，而是走出房间，高兴地大喊道，“我能看见了！我不用戴眼镜了！”
“你看，柏拉图，我不用戴眼镜了！”她弯下腰，一边抚摸着妈妈的毛绒拖鞋一边说道，“哎呀！”
露娜来到了厨房，她闻到了很香的味道。她拿起一个勺子放在了“一碗汤”里。
“露娜，你把勺子放在鱼缸里了！”妈妈说道。

[P10] 露娜从冰箱里拿出冰激凌，并往碗里舀了一些花生酱。然后，她还想在上面加一些巧克力酱。于是，她拿出一瓶酱开始挤，可是挤出的却是厚厚的一层番茄酱。
“真恶心！”她叫道。
露娜还是想吃些点心。“哦，饼干！”她边说边拿起来桌上一个打开的袋子。
正当她快要把猫食放进嘴里时，柏拉图把鼻子贴到了露娜的鼻子上，喵喵地叫了起来。
“哎呀！太恶心了！”
露娜又叫了起来。
一整天，露娜都在努力看清东西。不管她是眯着眼睛看，还是瞪大眼睛看，她眼里看到的都是一片模糊。当她被绊倒后，才看到人行道上那团模糊的东西是一双旱冰鞋。当她撞了上去，才发现卧室里那团模糊的东西原来是家具。最糟糕的是，她越想看清楚，她的头就越疼。最后她终于明白了，她的美梦并不是真的，她不戴眼镜还是看不清任何东西。

[P11] 露娜准备回房间睡觉，她嘲笑起自己来，于是唱道：
“吞拿鱼露娜戴眼镜，戴着它们到处走。”
回到房间就戴上了她的眼镜。
“哟，我又能看见了。”她叹了口气。
她向四周看了看，是的，她又能看清了。但是，她
并不那么高兴。

[P12] 露娜的爸爸听到
她上楼，便上来和她
道晚安。“露娜，你
没事吧？”他问道。
“我不知道，爸爸，我做了一个梦。”
露娜说道，“我梦到了月亮，还有巨大的
向日葵和小鱼。在梦里，我不用戴眼镜就能看清东西，我特别高兴，因为我看到的东西不再模糊。我知道我需要眼镜，可是，为什么家里只有我一个人需要戴眼镜呢？”
“哦，露娜，”爸爸说道，“你的眼睛跟我和妈妈还有克里斯汀的都不一样，你生下来眼睛就近视，你能看清近处的东西，但看不清远处的。眼镜上的镜片可以帮助你的眼睛聚焦。”

[P13] “除了戴眼镜，你身上还有很多与众不同的地方呢。”爸爸继续说道。
“什么与众不同的地方？”露娜吸了一下鼻子问道。
“嗯，比如你的个人魅力。”
“哦，爸爸。”
“还有你的智慧。你非常聪明，而且对什么都好奇。有时候，我真不知道如何回答你的问题！”
“还有，”爸爸继续说道，“我们家里只有你的名字是根据天上的一样东西取的，一样非常神奇的东西。”
“真的吗？”露娜不解地问道。

[P14] “当然了！露娜是月亮女神的名字。”
“我的名字是月亮？”露娜的脸上露出了喜悦。
“宝贝，信不信由你哟。”爸爸说道，“是这样的，在你出生前的一天，
我和你妈妈在装饰你的房间，我们做完时已将近午夜。于是，我们坐下来休息。那时，一轮满月挂在夜空，美丽的月光透过窗户洒满房间。我
们当时就决定你的名字就叫露娜。”
露娜听了兴奋不已，“你是说我的名字不是一条鱼？”
“当然不是了。”爸爸说道，“那么，我们再来谈谈你的眼镜……”
“没关系，爸爸，我不再介意戴着眼镜了。”
露娜拥抱了爸爸，然后钻进了被子。
“晚安，爸爸。”
“做个好梦，露娜。”

[P15] 露娜摘掉了眼镜，用她法兰绒睡衣的袖子擦了擦镜片。
柏拉图跳上了床，蜷缩在她身边。
露娜躺在床上，望着窗外又大又圆的月亮，周围的星星
闪闪发光。
不管戴不戴眼镜，
她的世界从未如此美丽！

[P3] Luna thought her name sounded like a fish, because it always made her think of 'Tuna Luna'.
Why can't my name be Alex, Rachel, or Sharon?

[P4] Luna loves her tabby cat, Plato, and her yellow shirt with curves and round patterns. She also loves the arched window in her bedroom, through which she can see the beautiful moon while sleeping. But Luna doesn't like her own name. There's one other thing she doesn't like, something she can't ignore:

Her glasses.

Those glasses sit on her nose, leaving faint indentations on her face. Luna chose a yellow frame with red polka dots at the eyewear store, matching her favorite shirt perfectly. Still, Luna doesn't like her glasses. Because when she looks in the mirror, the glasses almost cover her entire face.

[P5] She used her bangs to cover her glasses, so they wouldn't look so obvious.
She also pulled up her coat collar, trying to block her glasses.
She even walked with her head down. Of course, none of these worked very well.
"Ouch!"

[P6] Luna's mom opened a gift shop, and it had many strange things,
including a clock that walked backwards, and a string of lights that looked like cream-filled cookies. Customers
would always say, "That's simply incredible!"
Luna's mom didn't need to wear glasses,
her eyesight was very good.

[P7] Luna's dad is a high school math teacher, and his eyesight is also very good, so he doesn't need to wear glasses.
Even Luna's little sister, Kristen, doesn't wear glasses.
"I hate wearing glasses," Luna complained, "Even if they match my favorite clothes, my glasses are too noticeable. It's not fair!"

[P8] One night, Luna slept soundly. She dreamed she was on the moon, surrounded by giant sunflowers, with a pond nearby where many little fish were jumping in the water. When they jumped out of the water, Luna could clearly see every single fish.
In her dream, Luna wasn't wearing glasses, which made her especially happy.
"I can see! I don't need glasses!"

[P9] When Luna woke up, she didn't go looking for her glasses. Instead, she walked out of the room and shouted happily, "I can see! I don't need to wear glasses!"
"Look, Plato, I don't need to wear glasses!" she bent down, stroking her mom's fuzzy slippers and said, "Oh!"
Luna came to the kitchen. She smelled something delicious. She picked up a spoon and put it into the "bowl of soup."
"Luna, you put the spoon in the fish tank!" Mom said.

[P10] Luna took ice cream from the fridge and spooned some peanut butter into the bowl. Then, she wanted to add some chocolate sauce on top. So, she took out a bottle of sauce and started squeezing, but what came out was a thick layer of tomato sauce.
"Yuck!" she cried.
Luna still wanted some snacks. "Oh, cookies!" she said as she grabbed an open bag from the table.
Just as she was about to put cat food into her mouth, Plato pressed his nose against Luna's nose and meowed.
"Ew! That's disgusting!"
Luna cried out again.
All day, Luna struggled to see things clearly. Whether she squinted or widened her eyes, everything she saw was blurry. When she tripped, she finally saw that the blurry thing on the sidewalk was a pair of roller skates. When she bumped into it, she realized the blurry thing in her bedroom was actually furniture. Worst of all, the more she tried to see clearly, the more her head hurt. Finally, she understood: her dream wasn't real. Without her glasses, she still couldn't see anything clearly.

[P11] Luna was getting ready to go to her room to sleep. She laughed at herself and sang:
"Tuna Luna wears glasses, wearing them everywhere she goes."
She put on her glasses when she got back to her room.
"Oh, I can see again," she sighed.
She looked around. Yes, she could see clearly again. But she
wasn't very happy.

[P12] Luna's dad heard her come upstairs and came up to say goodnight. "Luna, are you okay?" he asked.
"I don't know, Dad, I had a dream," Luna said. "I dreamed of the moon, and huge sunflowers and little fish. In the dream, I could see everything clearly without glasses, and I was so happy because the things I saw were no longer blurry. I know I need glasses, but why is it only me in the family who needs to wear them?"
"Oh, Luna," Dad said, "your eyes are different from mine, your mom's, and Kristin's. You were born with nearsightedness—you can see things up close, but not things far away. The lenses in your glasses help your eyes focus."

[P13] "Besides wearing glasses, you have many unique qualities," Dad continued.
"What unique qualities?" Luna asked, sniffing.
"Well, like your personal charm."
"Oh, Dad."
"And your intelligence. You're very smart and curious about everything. Sometimes, I don't know how to answer your questions!"
"Also," Dad continued, "in our family, only your name is based on something in the sky, something very magical."
"Really?" Luna asked, puzzled.

[P14] "Of course! Luna is the name of the moon goddess."
"My name is the moon?" Luna's face lit up with joy.
"Sweetie, believe it or not," Dad said, "It was like this: the day before you were born, 
Mom and I were decorating your room. We finished around midnight. So, we sat down to rest. At that moment, a full moon hung in the sky, and beautiful moonlight streamed through the window, filling the room. We decided right then that your name would be Luna."
Luna was thrilled. "You mean my name isn't a fish?"
"Of course not," Dad said. "Now, let's talk about your glasses again..."
"It's okay, Dad, I don't mind wearing glasses anymore."
Luna hugged her dad and then snuggled into her blankets.
"Goodnight, Dad."
"Have a good dream, Luna."

[P15] Luna took off her glasses and wiped the lenses with the sleeve of her flannel pajamas.
Plato jumped onto the bed and curled up beside her.
Luna lay in bed, gazing at the big, round moon outside the window, with the stars sparkling around.
Whether she wore glasses or not,
her world had never been so beautiful!
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《戴眼镜的露娜》的封面，展示了主角露娜戴着大眼镜、抱着小猫的形象，并标注了作者、绘者、出版社及美国心理学会官方授权等信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《戴眼镜的露娜》的扉页，展示了书名、英文副标题、作者、绘者、译者、译校者及出版社信息，下方配有眼镜插图。
[P3] 本页描绘了露娜坐在窗边，旁边有一个鱼缸，她思考自己的名字像鱼，并疑惑为什么不能叫亚历克斯、雷切尔或莎伦。
[P4] 本页描述了露娜喜欢的物品和她不喜欢的两件事：自己的名字和她的眼镜。她选了一副与衬衫相配的黄色带红点眼镜，但仍然不喜欢，因为眼镜遮住了她的脸。
[P5] 露娜尝试用刘海、大衣领子和低头走路来隐藏她的眼镜，但这些方法都不太管用，最终她撞到了树上。
[P6] 本页描绘了露娜的妈妈经营一家充满奇趣物品的礼品店，顾客们对店里的倒走时钟和饼干灯感到惊叹，同时提到她视力很好，无需戴眼镜。
[P7] 本页介绍了露娜的爸爸和妹妹都不戴眼镜，露娜因此感到不公平，并再次表达了对戴眼镜的讨厌情绪。
[P8] 露娜在梦中来到月亮上，周围是向日葵和池塘里的小鱼，她能清楚地看见一切，因为梦里她没有戴眼镜，感到非常高兴。
[P9] 露娜醒来后以为自己不用戴眼镜了，兴奋地跑进厨房，却把勺子放进了鱼缸里，妈妈发现后提醒了她。
[P10] 露娜尝试吃冰激凌和饼干，却因误拿番茄酱和猫食而感到恶心；她一整天都在努力看清东西，但视线模糊，多次撞到物体，最终意识到不戴眼镜无法看清任何东西。
[P11] 露娜准备睡觉时，唱着自嘲的歌，回到房间戴上眼镜后虽然能看清了，但内心并不高兴。
[P12] 露娜向爸爸讲述她梦见自己不用戴眼镜就能看清一切，感到非常高兴，但同时也困惑为何只有自己需要戴眼镜。爸爸解释说她天生近视，眼镜能帮助她看清远处的东西。
[P13] 露娜的爸爸在她床边安慰她，指出她除了戴眼镜外还有很多与众不同的优点，如个人魅力、智慧和好奇心，并提到她的名字来源于天上的神奇之物，露娜对此感到好奇。
[P14] 爸爸向露娜解释了她名字的由来——在她出生前夜，满月的光辉洒满房间，父母因此为她取名露娜。露娜对此感到兴奋，并表示不再介意戴眼镜，最后在爸爸的祝福中入睡。
[P15] 露娜摘下眼镜，擦拭镜片后躺在床上，与猫咪柏拉图一起欣赏窗外的月亮和星星，感到世界无比美丽。
[P16] 画面中央是一个圆形鱼缸，里面有三条鱼，其中两条较大，一条较小，鱼缸内有气泡，背景为浅黄色。
